Label TWINSPAN Vegetation Surveys with Their Most Abundant Species

Source: R/denspe_twspn.R
denspe_twspn.Rd

Generates descriptive labels for vegetation surveys classified using the TWINSPAN (Two-Way Indicator Species Analysis) approach. Each survey identifier is supplemented with the names of its most abundant species, facilitating the floristic interpretation of TWINSPAN classifications and dendrograms.

Usage

denspe_twspn(
  nspe = 5,
  SpeAbund = NULL,
  dbClust = NULL,
  twin_ecan = NULL,
  sep = " | "
)

Arguments

nspe

Non-negative integer specifying the number of most abundant species to include in each survey label. Default is 5. If fewer ranked species are available, all available ranks are used. A value of 0 retains only the original survey identifiers.

SpeAbund

Optional data.frame produced by first_ten_species_twspn(), containing survey identifiers in the Survey column and ranked species in columns X1, X2, etc. If NULL, species rankings are calculated automatically.

dbClust

Numeric vegetation matrix or data.frame with surveys in rows and species in columns. If NULL, the vegetation data stored in twin_ecan$data are used.

twin_ecan

Optional fitted TWINSPAN object, typically produced by ecan::twinspan(). Used to retrieve the original vegetation data when dbClust is NULL and to validate survey identifiers.

sep

Character string separating the original survey identifier from the species names. Default is " | ".

Value

A numeric vegetation matrix retaining the original values and row order, but with modified row names containing the survey identifier and ranked species names.

The matrix also includes the attribute survey_labels, a data.frame containing:

Survey

Original survey identifier.

label

Generated survey label including species names.

Details

This function is designed as a supporting tool for vegetation classification based on TWINSPAN, particularly modified TWINSPAN implemented in the ecan package.

Species are ranked according to their abundance within each survey, using the results of first_ten_species_twspn(). The user can specify how many species should be included in the label.

For example, a survey originally identified as "R1" may receive the label "R1 | Festuca rubra | Agrostis capillaris" when nspe = 2.

The function does not perform or repeat TWINSPAN classification. Instead, it modifies the row names of the vegetation matrix for descriptive and graphical purposes.

Species-abundance information can be supplied directly through SpeAbund or calculated automatically from dbClust.

Survey identifiers are matched by name rather than row position, ensuring correct correspondence between the vegetation matrix and the abundance summary.

When a fitted TWINSPAN object is provided, the vegetation matrix must contain exactly the same surveys, although their order, species columns and abundance units may differ.

The resulting labels can be used with TWINSPAN plotting functions, such as plotClustAggregate_twspn(), to improve the ecological interpretation of vegetation groups.

See also

first_ten_species_twspn, plotClustAggregate_twspn, twinspan

Examples

# Example vegetation matrix
veg <- rbind(
  S1 = c(9, 5, 0, 0),
  S2 = c(8, 4, 1, 0),
  S3 = c(0, 1, 5, 8),
  S4 = c(0, 0, 4, 7)
)

colnames(veg) <- c(
  "Species A", "Species B",
  "Species C", "Species D"
)

# Modified TWINSPAN classification
tw <- ecan::twinspan(
  veg,
  modified = TRUE,
  n_clusters = 2,
  min_size = 2,
  polish = "hill",
  species = FALSE
)

# Identify the most abundant species
top <- first_ten_species_twspn(twin_ecan = tw)

# Label each survey with its two most abundant species
labelled <- denspe_twspn(
  nspe = 2,
  SpeAbund = top,
  twin_ecan = tw
)

# Inspect the resulting labels
rownames(labelled)
#> [1] "S1 | Species A 9 | Species B 5" "S2 | Species A 8 | Species B 4"
#> [3] "S3 | Species D 8 | Species C 5" "S4 | Species D 7 | Species C 4"

# Retrieve the original and modified survey identifiers
attr(labelled, "survey_labels")
#>   Survey                          label
#> 1     S1 S1 | Species A 9 | Species B 5
#> 2     S2 S2 | Species A 8 | Species B 4
#> 3     S3 S3 | Species D 8 | Species C 5
#> 4     S4 S4 | Species D 7 | Species C 4
